title: Gases in air sheet
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Ecosystems (7D); atoms, elements and molecules (7H)
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 58 (Gases in air sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 58: The air we breathe. To understand that air is a mixture of elements and compounds in fixed proportions

questions.q: Out of 100 litres of air, how many litres are nitrogen?
questions.model: Nitrogen is 78% of air. 78% of 100 = 78. So about 78 litres.

questions.q: Is carbon dioxide an element or a compound?
Why is air a mixture, not a compound?
questions.a: The gases are not chemically joined

questions.q: Draw and label a pie chart of the gases in air. Under it, list each gas as element or compound and give one use.
questions.a: Correct chart and labels; nitrogen, oxygen, argon elements; CO2 and water vapour compounds
questions.model: Teacher draws the nitrogen sector (just over three quarters) and labels it '78%: element'.

questions.q: How many litres of oxygen are in 500 litres of air?
Why might a sealed room feel stuffy after many hours?
questions.a: Oxygen is used and carbon dioxide and water vapour build up

questions.q: Big question: what is most of each breath made of?
